_README: Written-down ground truth that a generated document must not contradict.
docs/todo.md item 2b. This is a FIXTURE, not configuration: every entry
should come from an observed failure and should cite where the truth was
established, so a later reader can re-argue the fact rather than trusting
Why it exists: the agent's own fact-check step makes documents WORSE. Asked
to 'create with fact checked infos', run 4d97aa60 fetched four sources and
produced fruiting temperatures of 14-21 C on a tropical species -- the
Pleurotus ostreatus cold-shock rule -- while the plain 'create a document'
run acba4766 got it roughly right. Retrieval actively drags the answer
toward the wrong species, and both bad documents titled themselves 'Fact
Checked & Corrected'. An agent fact-check is a prompt to go look, never a
verdict; this file is the part that can actually be checked.
REPORT-ONLY, like config/field_semantics.json. Findings reach the closing
summary and nothing else. See docs/todo.md item 8 before changing that.

subjects.name: Pink oyster (Pleurotus djamor)
subjects.source: docs/resolvedissues.md, "4B retired -- 2026-07-18". Established by scoring six same-task runs against cultivation sources, not by a single lookup.

ranges.note: Run 009660d2 stated 20-24 C for colonization and then instructed a further drop.
The load-bearing number. 14-21 C (run 4d97aa60) and 16-20 C (the 4B) are the P. ostreatus range applied to a tropical species. 26 C, which 4d97aa60 flagged as too warm, is squarely optimal.
Scoped to fruiting deliberately. The ground truth as recorded says only 'RH 85-95%'; 60-70% during colonization is ordinary practice, so applying it to every phase would fire on correct documents.

At 3-6 air changes per hour. Only prescriptive ranges are judged -- '<1000 ppm' is a bound that contains this one, while the 4B's '1000-1500 ppm through fruiting' is backwards. No run has ever caught the CO2 error, which is the most consequential mistake in the set.

contradictions.why: P. djamor is thermophilic and needs no cold shock. A numeric drop instruction is the failure that retired the 4B and it reached chamber setpoints twice more on the 9B. A general remark that cooling can help pinning is NOT this -- the damage is a prescribed delta. The verb must act on a temperature: 'lower accuracy (±2°C)' in a sensor datasheet matched an earlier, looser pattern.
contradictions.message: P. djamor is thermophilic and needs no cold shock; this prescribes one, and a chamber setpoint is what it becomes.

contradictions.why: Exactly backwards: P. djamor is the warm-loving member of the genus.
contradictions.seen_in: 009660d2: "pink oysters prefer slightly cooler than other Pleurotus species during fruiting"
contradictions.message: Backwards — P. djamor is the warm-loving member of the genus. This is the claim that retired the 4B.

contradictions.why: Warns against a temperature inside the fruiting range. 26 C was flagged as yield-reducing in a document that called itself fact-checked.
contradictions.message: Warns against a temperature that is inside the recorded fruiting range of 20–30 °C.

requires.why: A cultivation document that specifies temperature and humidity for fruiting and says nothing about CO2 has omitted the parameter the model gets wrong most often. Run 4d97aa60 dropped it entirely after four source fetches.
requires.message: a cultivation document that gives temperature and humidity for fruiting and says nothing about CO₂ has omitted the parameter the model gets wrong most often; run 4d97aa60 dropped it entirely after four source fetches.
